{{Short description|Learned society}}
The '''Latvian Mathematical Society''' (in [[Latvian Language|Latvian]]: ''Latvijas Matemātikas Biedrība'', '''LMB''') is a [[learned society]] of mathematicians from [[Latvia]], recognized by the [[International Mathematical Union]] as the national mathematical organization for its country.<ref>[http://www.mathunion.org/members/countries/list/sorted-by-names/latvia/ Latvia] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171010194627/http://www.mathunion.org/members/countries/list/sorted-by-names/latvia/ |date=2017-10-10 }}, [[International Mathematical Union]], retrieved 2015-01-24.</ref> Its goals are stimulating mathematical activity in Latvia while consolidating the former achievements, and it has the responsibility of representing the Latvian mathematicians at the international level.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www-history.mcs.st-andrews.ac.uk/Societies/alph_list.html|title=Alphabetical List of Mathematical Societies|work=st-andrews.ac.uk}}</ref> It was founded in 1993.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www-history.mcs.st-andrews.ac.uk/Societies/Latvian.html|title=The Latvian Mathematical Society|accessdate=January 24, 2015|publisher=[[University of St Andrews]]| date=August 2004 }}</ref><ref>{{citation|journal=European Mathematical Society Newsletter|date=June 2003|title=Latvian Mathematical Society after 10 years|first=Alexander|last=Šostak|url=http://www.mathematics.lv/lms_10_years_after.pdf|pages=21–25}}.</ref>

The current president is [[Andrejs Reinfelds]], from the [[University of Latvia]], [[Riga]].
